learningObjective: Identify the precondition set that a compiler must satisfy to vectorize a loop safely and effectively.

canonicalClaims.claim: A loop is vectorizable when there is no cross-iteration WRITE dependence into the same location; cross-iteration READS of already-defined values are legal but may require shifted / unaligned loads and a tail (masked or scalar) epilogue for non-multiple trip counts.
conditions: No loop-carried write-write or write-read dependences within the vectorization window.
The vector unit or ISA supports unaligned or shifted vector loads.
The tail block is handled explicitly (masking or scalar fallback).
nonImplications: Does not imply vectorization always improves performance; memory-bound loops gain little.
Does not imply zero cost for shifted loads on every ISA.

misconceptions.claim: Any cross-iteration read of an array is a loop-carried dependence that blocks vectorization.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Loop-carried dependences that block vectorization involve writes, not reads; reads of values written in earlier iterations (of the same loop) are true dependences only if the write is also inside the loop.

misconceptions.claim: Vectorization of a pointwise loop is illegal when FP32 multiplication is used because of non-associativity.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Associativity concerns apply to reduction reordering, not pointwise elementwise vectorization.

misconceptions.claim: If the array is 32-byte aligned at index 0, all vector loads are automatically aligned regardless of the shift.
misconceptions.whyWrong: A shifted read (e.g., A[i-1]) starts at a different alignment offset; the compiler must emit an unaligned load or a shift/blend across two aligned loads.

misconceptions.claim: The vectorizer will refuse any loop whose trip count is not a multiple of the vector width.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Modern vectorizers produce a masked or scalar epilogue for the tail iterations; non-multiple trip counts do not block vectorization.

implementationFacts: LLVM's loop vectorizer inserts masked or scalar epilogue loops.
AVX2 supports 8-lane FP32; AVX-512 supports 16-lane FP32.
GPU SIMT effectively performs 32-lane vectorization at the warp level.
performanceScenarios: A shifted stencil A[i-1] + 2*A[i] + A[i+1] vectorizes to two unaligned loads plus one aligned load + FMAs.
